title: Explore whether investment banking is right for you
details: Learn how a bank is organised (IBD, Sales & Trading, Research), what analysts actually do, and talk to upperclassmen who recruited for IB.

title: Apply to diversity and early insight programs
details: Applications are due at the end of the fall semester. These programs run ahead of regular recruiting, so start interview prep earlier, and interviews are sometimes accelerated. See the Programs tab for specific programs.

title: Attend early insight programs, then keep preparing
details: Diversity and early insight programs take place early in the calendar year. Keep up interview preparation afterwards.

title: Confirm IB is the right path before recruiting ramps up
details: If you didn't explore IB as a freshman, do it now: recruiting runs through sophomore fall and spring.

title: Network with upperclassmen and alumni
details: Cold calls, coffee chats and info sessions. Research each person first and lead the conversation with good questions.

title: Build your behavioral and technical interview skills
details: Know every common behavioral question. For technicals, work through the M&I 400 guide: valuation methods, DCF (WACC, CAPM, Beta), EBITDA, LBOs, enterprise vs. equity value, and how the three statements connect.

title: Keep up with markets, current events and deal flow
details: Follow the major indices, market news and each target firm's recent deals so you can talk about them in interviews.

title: Submit applications and attend recruiting events
details: Fill out applications and go to both Vanderbilt and non-Vanderbilt recruiting events.

title: Prepare for the interview process
details: Typical sequence: HireVue, then a first round (phone or on campus), then a Superday of 3–5 back-to-back interviews.

title: Protect your GPA
details: Aim for 3.87+ in A&S or Peabody, or ideally 3.7+ in Engineering.

title: Get involved on campus and take on leadership
details: Firms look for meaningful experiences with clear personal impact, plus teamwork, leadership and initiative.

title: Attend case workshops and firm events
details: Start learning how case interviews work and meet the firms early.

title: Build experience through internships, projects or organizations
details: Anything that shows structured problem solving, quantitative work and impact.

title: Develop your "why consulting" and "why this firm" answers
details: You'll use these in networking conversations and interviews.

title: Attend info sessions and networking events
details: Build relationships, understand each firm and get noticed early.

title: Apply to early programs where eligible
details: For example Bain BEL/CREW, BCG Embark/Advance and A&M CCDP. Check the Programs tab for deadlines and eligibility.

title: Attend info sessions and networking events
details: Build relationships, understand each firm and get noticed early.

title: Apply to early programs where eligible
details: For example Bain BEL/CREW, BCG Embark/Advance and A&M CCDP. Check the Programs tab for deadlines and eligibility.

title: Start case prep and get your resume and stories ready
details: Start heavily networking and case prepping, attend every recruiting event, and have your resume and behavioral examples ready before applications open.

title: Network heavily with consultants and recruiters
details: December through January/February is the key window. Attend recruiting dinners and events.

title: Case prep heavily and prepare behavioral examples
details: MBA case books are recommended. Practice profitability, market sizing, market entry and M&A cases. CaseCoach is free through Vanderbilt.

title: Finalize your resume before spring applications open
details: In the 2026 cycle applications opened mid-February.

title: Apply for internships
details: Deadlines moved from July to March this cycle and are expected to move earlier again. Example cycle: applications opened Feb 15 and closed Mar 29.

title: Complete online assessments
details: McKinsey Solve, Bain TestGorilla or BCG Casey. Aim for the 9th or 10th decile on Solve and Casey. In the example cycle, the Solve invite came 3 days after the deadline and was due a week later.

title: First and final round interviews
details: First round: case and behavioral interviews. Final round: more cases and behavioral, usually in person. It moves fast: in the example cycle, round 1 was April 17 and the offer came April 24. Be ready before applications open.

title: Practice technical interview skills consistently
details: Getting good takes time. Use LeetCode for coding interviews and Quantable for quant. Practice explaining your thinking out loud, since interviewers judge how you approach problems as much as the answer.

title: Build relationships that can lead to referrals
details: Most people apply with only a resume and a referral; cover letters are rare. A referral helps you get the first interview, and after that only your ability matters.

title: Prepare for quant interviews
details: Expect probability, brainteaser and data-analysis questions (e.g. the coin-flip problem in the Tech guide). Quantable and r/quantfinance are good places to start.

title: Quant recruiting opens
details: Quant firms recruit starting late spring at the end of sophomore year: up to 8 technical rounds, usually at most 1 behavioral, and an in-person superday. Track openings with the Northwestern Fintech quant internship list.

title: Get ready for Big Tech recruiting
details: Big Tech recruiting starts in late summer going into junior year. Have your resume and referrals lined up.

title: Apply and interview for Big Tech internships
details: Typically 2–3 technical rounds and 1–2 behavioral, including a superday. The SimplifyJobs internship list tracks openings.

title: Watch for AI lab and startup openings
details: AI labs and startups recruit at any time, and processes vary heavily.
